name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 3 No 17

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 3

clue.text: Note’s sound (basic note) for pieces by stars of the 10

definitions.note: the answer names a troupe of comic film actors

blocks.note: the bracketed hint says which note: the basic note of a piece of music is its key, plus the 's
a tone is a musical sound
coppers are pennies, small pieces of money; cops is the short form of coppers

explanation.surface: A music lesson about the sound of a keynote, written as pieces for star performers.
explanation.walkthrough: '(basic note)' glosses the first note as the key of a piece. The 10 is the cross-reference to 10-down, SILENT SCREEN; the Keystone Cops were bumbling policemen in Mack Sennett's silent comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Keystone Cops were a famous troupe of slapstick policemen in early silent comedy films, so they were stars of that era.

clue.text: How to rouse birds: Shakespeare’s way, not ours?

definitions.text: How to rouse birds: Shakespeare’s way, not ours?

blocks.note: surface reading: a practical question about waking birds from their perches
setter's reading: the verb is one Shakespeare used in The Winter's Tale and modern English has dropped

explanation.surface: A bird-keeper asks how to wake birds, noting Shakespeare did it differently.
explanation.walkthrough: The word literally means to turn birds off their roost; Shakespeare coined 'unroosted' in The Winter's Tale, and it has not survived into everyday English.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive birds from their perch is literally to undo their roosting, an archaic verb found in Shakespearean English.

clue.text: Light weight matter for sea beast

blocks.note: a gram is a small metric unit of weight
matter is an old word for pus, as in a wound that is discharging matter

explanation.surface: A physics note on a light weight of material, oddly attached to a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like physical substance, but here it is the medical sense of discharge from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The grampus is a sea mammal, a name given to Risso's dolphin and formerly to the killer whale.

clue.text: Translate light weight to beat severely

blocks.note: TR is the standard abbreviation for translate or translated
an ounce is a small imperial weight

explanation.surface: An instruction to convert a light weight into a heavy beating.
explanation.walkthrough: TR for translate is a dictionary abbreviation, as in 'tr. by' on a title page.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to defeat or thrash them heavily, which is beating them severely.

clue.text: Royal Scots college wholly in grip of some science

indicators.note: being held in the grip of something means being enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: BIOL is the usual short form of biology, one science among several
wholly means all of it

explanation.surface: A college linked to the Scottish royals is entirely devoted to science.
explanation.walkthrough: Balliol College, Oxford, takes its name from John de Balliol, whose son John Balliol became King of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford college bears the name of the Balliol family, which supplied a medieval king of Scotland, hence its royal Scottish link.

clue.text: Weapon to go through predatorily

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-barrelled gun
second meaning: to search hastily through something in order to steal

explanation.walkthrough: The noun and the verb are spelt the same; the verb is the one used of burglars going through drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a shouldered firearm and a verb meaning to ransack a place looking for things to steal.

clue.text: Gone bad? Add salt and pepper, not in July or August?

blocks.note: food that has gone bad is said to be off
to season food is to add salt and pepper to it

explanation.surface: A cook rescuing spoiled food with seasoning, outside the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is consistent throughout, but the question mark warns that the last part is a definition by example: high summer is the peak holiday time.
explanation.definitionFit: July and August are the peak holiday months, so anything happening outside them falls in the quieter, low-demand part of the year.

clue.text: English, Welsh fashion, before Lords in Commons?

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase for a place, the answer an adverb

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the word before it is remodelled

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written, to be rearranged
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A comparison of English and Welsh styles in Parliament, Lords before Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: By convention members of the House of Commons do not name the House of Lords but call it 'another place', so the Lords, spoken of in the Commons, are somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Commons custom refers to the upper house only obliquely as another place, which amounts to saying it is located somewhere other than here.

clue.text: Lots of people had a day here with the Marx brothers

definitions.text: Lots of people had a day here with the Marx brothers

blocks.clueFragment: Lots of people had a day here
blocks.note: surface reading: a popular outing spot where crowds spend a day
setter's reading: the Marx Brothers film 'A Day at the ...' names the place, a horse-racing meeting

explanation.surface: Crowds enjoying a day out in the company of the Marx Brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1937 Marx Brothers comedy is titled A Day at the Races, so the place where the day was had is the race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A race meeting is a classic day out for crowds, and the Marx Brothers film title spends its day at one.

clue.text: Sennett’s work makes a century (see table)

indicators.note: a work made from the name treats its letters as raw material to be rearranged

blocks.note: the surname of Mack Sennett, the producer behind Keystone comedies, without the apostrophe-s

explanation.surface: A tribute to Mack Sennett's hundredth film.
explanation.walkthrough: Mack Sennett produced the Keystone comedies, keeping the silent-screen theme. '(see table)' points to the ten times table.
explanation.definitionFit: In the multiplication table, ten multiplied by ten gives one hundred, which is a century.

clue.text: Giant upset by a spider

definitions.note: the answer is the giant's name, not a word for giant

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge creature frightened by a small spider.
explanation.walkthrough: Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, who imprisons Christian and Hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress the monstrous jailer of Doubting Castle is named Giant Despair.

clue.text: Wood filmed at 4 port with an altered direction

definitions.note: the definition names an actress by her surname; the answer is her first name

indicators.note: changing the direction of travel means reading the letters the other way

blocks.note: the port on the Red Sea in the region of Israel that is the answer to 4-down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film shot at a southern Israeli harbour, its route changed.
explanation.walkthrough: Natalie Wood was the Hollywood film actress; 'Wood filmed' looks like timber being photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie Wood starred in many films, so the actress Wood who was filmed has this first name.

clue.text: Beatles’ words that go well with Michelle, another fancy girl’s name

definitions.text: Beatles’ words that go well with Michelle

blocks.clueFragment: Beatles’ words that go well with Michelle
blocks.note: first meaning: the French words for 'my beauty' that follow the name in the Beatles song
second meaning: a fanciful girl's name, run together into one word

explanation.surface: A note on Beatles lyrics that rhyme with a girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles song Michelle pairs the name with the French endearment meaning 'my beautiful one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles lyric sets the French endearment beside Michelle, and the same letters run together make an ornate girl's name.

clue.text: Persecute Archbishop, academic, and star of 10

blocks.note: to harry is to harass or persecute
Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Someone harasses a churchman, a scholar and a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop is a specific one, Cosmo Gordon Lang of Canterbury, contemporary with the silent era.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Langdon was a leading comedian of silent films in the 1920s, a star of the silent screen.

clue.text: Lark about at start of 14 with star of 10

indicators.note: to lark about is to fool around, so the letters fool around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening word of the answer to 14-across, OFF-SEASON

explanation.surface: Fooling around as the season begins, alongside a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Karloff began in silent films before becoming famous as Frankenstein's monster, so he was a star of that era.

clue.text: First among solvers to end sadly in African capital

indicators.note: something going sadly has gone wrong, so the letters before it are disarranged

blocks.note: politeness puts the other person first, so the solver is named first in a pair
the single letter E added to finish the fodder

explanation.surface: A crossword competition ends badly in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Araucaria parse: the solver comes first in 'you and ...', and E is tacked on to complete the letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon in west-central Africa.

clue.text: Leo and litter, perhaps, in The Young Lions

definitions.text: Leo and litter, perhaps, in The Young Lions

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the words are only a possible version, so the letters may be arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lion and her cubs cast in a film called The Young Lions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says a lion (Leo) and its cubs (a litter) would be the parts named in a film titled The Young Lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A part named in a work's own title is called that, and young lions would be exactly the characters such a title names.

clue.text: Region of Israel, for example, in prominent feature

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: neb is a dialect word for a nose or beak, the most prominent feature of a face
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A geography note: a region of Israel is an example of a prominent landscape feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Negeb is an older spelling of the Negev, the desert in southern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev, also spelt Negeb, is the large desert region forming the southern half of Israel.

clue.text: Prince Hal (Hal in charge), potentially a star of 10

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's young Prince Hal, given command, as a possible future film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket adds a second HAL and the letters for 'in charge' to the fodder; all of it is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin, the tramp in a bowler hat, was the most famous comedian of silent films.

clue.text: Prince Hal’s friend keeps twopence for Mary

definitions.note: the definition is a first name; the answer is the surname that goes with it

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Poins is Prince Hal's companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
two lots of p, the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Prince Hal's companion holds on to a little money for a girl called Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Poppins is the magical nanny of P. L. Travers's books and the Disney film, so Mary's surname completes her name.

clue.text: Spooner’s last stander defeated by star of the 10

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words are exchanged

blocks.note: General Custer made the famous Last Stand at the Little Bighorn, and defeated means beaten; swapping the C and B sounds of that pair gives the name

explanation.surface: Spooner's final defender beaten by a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of 'Custer beaten' to hear the comedian's name; the vowel of the second word is spelt differently in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton, the stone-faced comedian of The General, was one of the great stars of silent films.

clue.text: Bygone entertainment is wrong about fast fallen debris under cliff

indicators.note: something placed about another goes round it, enclosing what follows

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
scree is the loose broken rock that collects at the foot of a cliff

explanation.surface: Old-time entertainment was spoiled by rubble falling below a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is wrong' reads as a verdict, but 'is' only joins, and 'wrong' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent cinema, before synchronised sound arrived around 1927, is a form of entertainment that belongs to the past.

clue.text: Point, for example, may be silly; I’m for WC myself

definitions.text: Point, for example, may be silly

blocks.clueFragment: Point, for example, may be silly
blocks.note: first meaning: point is a cricket fielding position, and silly point is the close-in version
second meaning: a fan of the comedian W. C. Fields would call himself his man

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point is a fielding position beside the batter and 'silly point' stands dangerously close. W. C. Fields was a film comedian, not a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed at point is one of the fielding side, and a supporter of W. C. Fields is, split in two, a Fields man.

clue.text: Star in a whirl: he’d have been wasted on the 10

definitions.text: he’d have been wasted on the 10

indicators.note: letters set in a whirl are spun round and land in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity in a frenzy, whose talents would have been lost on old films.
explanation.walkthrough: Silent films had no soundtrack, so a singer's voice could not be heard in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra's fame rested on his singing voice, which films without sound could never have shown off.

clue.text: Dealer’s partner, West, a lady that eats fish

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside itself

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for West
her is the pronoun for a woman
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A card dealer's partner seated West, alongside a woman eating fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge table picture (West, partner, dealer) is a decoy; the phrase is 'wheeler-dealer', a shrewd operator.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom wheeler-dealer pairs the two words, so this is the word that partners dealer in that phrase.

clue.text: Girl and man — American, one could gather from Citizen Kane

definitions.text: one could gather from Citizen Kane
definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing a word; the answer is that word

blocks.note: Rose is a girl's name
bud, short for buddy, is an American way of addressing a man

explanation.surface: A couple, a girl and an American man, met through Citizen Kane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' plays on 'gather ye rosebuds' and on gathering meaning from Kane's dying word, the name of his childhood sled.
explanation.definitionFit: Kane's dying utterance in Orson Welles's film is the mystery the story investigates, and rosebuds are also flowers one gathers.

clue.text: See 5
The lady’s going to hold an egg

blocks.note: first meaning: the contraction for 'she will'
second meaning: the hard casing that holds an egg

explanation.surface: A woman is about to pick up an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the apostrophe in the first meaning: 'she will' contracts to a word spelt the same as the egg's casing.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of she will sounds and spells the same as the hard outer case enclosing an egg.
